## Parent feature and area

<!-- Link the parent feature issue and add this task to its child list.
Area: Frontend / Backend / Integration.
Owner: name or Unassigned. Identify both human approvers for shared work. -->

## Stage and flags

Stage: Backlog
Flags: None

<!-- Stages: Backlog / Ready / In progress / Review / Done.
Flags: Paused (deliberate hold), Blocked (dependency/decision), or both.
For each flag record reason, linked issue/decision, responsible person where known,
and what allows resumption. Keep the actual stage while flagged.
Meet readiness and approval requirements before starting or resuming work. -->

## Outcome and scope

<!-- Describe the concrete outcome and known boundaries, not an exhaustive implementation plan.
Explain why this task is needed, especially when discovered after initial planning.
Unknown details may remain Pending at issue creation. -->

## Specifications and plan

<!-- Link relevant product/technical spec sections, acceptance criterion IDs,
and implementation plan/task IDs when available. Mark draft versus approved versions.
Keep requirements authoritative in the specs and execution steps in the plan. -->

## Acceptance criteria

<!-- List observable outcomes for this task and map them to feature criteria.
Identify the task's contribution without claiming the entire feature is complete. -->

## Interfaces, dependencies and open questions

<!-- Link shared contracts and blocking task issues. Record questions and affected work.
Frontend fixtures can support parallel development against an agreed contract, but
do not establish real backend integration. Name any later integration task needed. -->

## Verification and handoffs

<!-- Identify relevant tests/checks and required review checkpoints for this task.
Testing agents own tests/fixtures/test configuration; implementers own production code.
Include test-readiness review, implementation/coverage review, and final feature security
where applicable, or link the task owning that checkpoint and explain the dependency.
Use actual target-stack commands once selected; do not require every test layer for every task. -->

## Readiness and approval

<!-- Before implementation starts, record:
- Assigned owner and applicable human approver(s).
- Approved scope/specification/plan references and explicit task authorisation.
- Relevant agreed contracts, resolved prerequisites, and allowed file ownership.
- Acceptance checks and required review handoffs.
Pending items prevent dependent work from starting, not issue creation or unrelated ready work.
Issue status or assignment alone does not grant implementation approval. -->

## Decisions and corrections

<!-- Record dated decisions and approval references as needed.
New scope or shared-interface changes require applicable human approval.
Every failed-loop code/test edit requires an approved correction plan. Record the shared
cycle count and related task IDs: two cycles per reviewed batch, not two per issue.
Preserve completed plan entries; authorised follow-up tasks do not reset that count. -->

## Completion evidence

<!-- Link PRs and record criterion -> evidence, actual checks/results, required reviews,
documentation updates, and remaining limitations. Distinguish passed, failed and unverified.
Close only when this task's acceptance and required handoffs are satisfied.
The parent stays open until all required tasks and feature-level acceptance checks pass. -->
